description: Use this when the person wants something people use: upload a photo, generate or transform pictures with AI, accounts or sign-in, saved data, a tool, a calculator, a game, bookings, a dashboard. Pass their request as they said it; never turn it into a landing page. An app that makes pictures with AI asks for the owner's own image-AI key; it never fakes results. Pass the customer's brief in the customer's own words; do not add features the customer did not ask for (no invented sign-up, accounts, subscriptions or payments). When it is built Pugi checks it for security issues, and publish waits for that check. An app that needs a server or a database moves onto Pugi's servers on its own; the person stays in this chat. In hosts that render the build card (MCP Apps or ChatGPT widget), the card tracks progress automatically: do not poll job_status. In hosts without a build card (Claude Code or API), call job_status with the job_id until the job is finished, stopped or failed. Do not use for a simple website (use build_site) or to change an app already built here (use edit).

brief.description: The app to build, in the customer's own words.

brief_confirmed.description: True only after the person has seen the summary and agreed. In a chat, without it nothing starts and the summary comes back.

brief_version.description: With brief_confirmed: the version of the summary the person agreed to, as returned with that summary.

idempotency_key.description: A unique string naming this build. Reuse it only to retry the same call; it is never charged twice.

language.description: The language the person is writing in, as a BCP 47 tag such as "ru".

max_usd.description: The most this build may cost in USD (default 5).

site_language.description: Language for the app content; independent of the chat card language.

without_logo.description: True only when the person said this site should not use the logo they picked.

name: build_app
title: Build a web app
